title: Oil above 105 dollars, a hawkish Fed and an RBI cash drain hand Dalal Street a fifth straight weekly loss
standfirst: Crude oil surging on West Asia supply fears was the story of the week, dragging the Nifty and Sensex to a fifth consecutive weekly fall, pushing the rupee to about 95.5 per dollar and lifting India's 10-year bond yield above 7 percent. The RBI spent the week draining surplus liquidity and selling dollars, while hot US inflation flipped expectations from a Fed rate cut to a near-certain hike and the ECB raised rates to 2.5 percent. The weekend brought the RBI's order forcing Tata Sons to list, which the group is expected to fight in court, a BRICS summit in New Delhi, and a Saudi pipeline shutdown that keeps oil supply tight into the Fed week.

items.text: The Nifty fell 2.1 percent to 23,398.10 and the Sensex 2.3 percent to 74,781.76, a fifth straight weekly loss, as crude oil, rising US yields and the RBI's liquidity drain weighed on sentiment. Metal stocks fell up to 5 percent, HDFC Bank hit a 52-week low and the Nifty broke below its 23,900 to 24,000 support.

The rupee logged its sharpest weekly fall in four months, sliding past 95.5 to 95.55, even as the RBI sold dollars and used FX swaps to slow the decline, and India's 10-year yield crossed 7 percent after a trimmed debt auction.

The RBI drained surplus banking cash through a 26-day VRRR auction and OMO bond sales, Governor Malhotra said nothing is off the table on liquidity and the rupee, and August retail inflation is estimated at a 20-month high near 4.9 percent, narrowing room for an October rate cut.

SEBI's month-old closing auction session produced 1,000-point Sensex swings on expiry day, prompting a weekend consultation paper that could keep the old settlement method for a year. SEBI and the RBI also launched a Demat 2.0 pilot and MSE settled India's first tokenised corporate bond.

The RBI rejected Tata Sons' bid to stay an unlisted NBFC, a decision the group is expected to challenge in court, while HDFC Bank sent two names to the RBI for its next CEO, NSE cut its IPO to about Rs 22,569 crore ahead of an eleven-issue week, and Adani Ports settled disclosure proceedings with SEBI.

Brent crude surged past 105 dollars and neared 110 midweek on unresolved West Asia tensions, ending the week up 9.5 percent at 104.61 dollars. Saudi Arabia then shut the East-West pipeline it uses to bypass Hormuz after drone attacks from Iraq, and Iran said the strait reopens only on its terms.

US consumer inflation rose 3.4 percent year on year in August, pushing the odds of a Fed hike at the September 16-17 meeting to about 90 percent. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.97 percent, its highest since 2023.
The ECB raised rates to 2.5 percent and President Lagarde said the inflation shock will be longer lasting, with policymakers warning high oil could force further hikes.

Wall Street ended the week lower despite a Friday rebound, with the S&P 500 down 1.2 percent and the Dow down 2.1 percent, while Japan's Nikkei lost 1.6 percent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng 3.3 percent. Gold fell 1.8 percent.

India hosted the BRICS summit, where leaders adopted a unanimous declaration opposing carbon border taxes and unilateral tariffs but ruled out a common currency, and Modi held talks with Putin and Xi. Canada sought EU associate membership as its trade war with the US deepened, and Washington finalised duties on Indian solar panels.

watch: The Fed's September 16-17 meeting, with a hike priced at about 90 percent, and the Bank of Japan's decision in the same week.
